title: Parameter Folding: Reducing Model Size Through Redundancy Elimination
text: Parameter folding optimization technique reduces model size removing dimensions parameters dimensions contain redundant (repeated) values. can significantly reduce: Model file size (.mod .dat files) Memory usage model generation solving Solve time reducing number non-zero coefficients

title: Parameter Folding: Reducing Model Size Through Redundancy Elimination
text: Many energy system models parameters indexed multiple dimensions, dimension combinations actually used. example: equations reference folded parameter, slice index simply omitted:
code: # Original parameter: 5D with 1080 rows pTechCinp2use{tech, comm, region, year, slice}  # But if values are constant across 'slice' dimension: pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, SPRING] = 0.95 pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, SUMMER] = 0.95 pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, AUTUMN] = 0.95 pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, WINTER] = 0.95  # Can be folded to: 4D with 90 rows (12x compression) pTechCinp2use{tech, comm, region, year} pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025] = 0.95 # Before folding: vTechInp[t,c,r,y,s] >= pTechCinp2use[t,c,r,y,s] * vTechAct[t,r,y,s]  # After folding: vTechInp[t,c,r,y,s] >= pTechCinp2use[t,c,r,y] * vTechAct[t,r,y,s]

title: Parameter Folding: Reducing Model Size Through Redundancy Elimination
text: energyRt models entity-specific mappings, use create_fold_spec(): Key concepts: Validation mappings: Specify entity mapping (e.g., mTechSlice) use validating folding safe Mapping chains: parameters requiring multi-hop validation (e.g., storage parameters need mStorageComm → mCommSlice) Automatic detection: function analyzes parameter’s data determine values constant across dimension
code: fold_spec <- create_fold_spec(   model,   fold_dims = list(     slice = list(       tech = 'mTechSlice',      # Technology parameters use mTechSlice mapping       sup = 'mSupSlice',        # Supply parameters use mSupSlice mapping       comm = 'mCommSlice',      # Commodity parameters use mCommSlice mapping       stg = c('mStorageComm', 'mCommSlice')  # Storage uses chain: storage→comm→slice     )   ) )  # View foldable parameters cat("Foldable parameters:", sum(fold_spec$can_fold), "\n")

title: Parameter Folding: Reducing Model Size Through Redundancy Elimination
text: Folding safe values constant across dimension relevant entity. validation mapping specifies entities check:
code: # For technology parameter with dims {tech, comm, region, year, slice} # Check if values constant across slice FOR EACH tech  # Using mTechSlice (which techs have slice variation): FOR EACH (tech, comm, region, year) group:   - If tech is in mTechSlice: SKIP (needs slice detail)   - Otherwise: check if all slice values are identical    # If all groups pass → can fold

text: dimension appears multiple times different roles: folding algorithm preserves duplicate dimension names active_dims keeps original data columns (excluding folded dimension).

text: Group data dimensions EXCEPT one folded group, check values constant (within tolerance) Uses dplyr::n_distinct() count unique values per group Alias handling: Groups any_of(dims_with_aliases) handle aliased column names

title: Parameter Folding: Reducing Model Size Through Redundancy Elimination
text: group, check relevant entity validation mapping entity mapping (e.g., tech mTechSlice): SKIP (needs detail) entity mapping: values must constant Ensures don’t fold away required detail Example:
code: # mTechSlice = {E01, E21}  (these techs vary by slice) # mTechSlice mapping: {(E01, ANNUAL), (E21, ANNUAL)}  # For pTechCinp2use group (RHO, ..., ...): # - RHO not in mTechSlice → can fold ✓  # For group (E01, ..., ...): # - E01 in mTechSlice → SKIP, cannot fold for this tech # - But ALL groups need to pass, so entire parameter cannot fold  # UNLESS: E01 values are actually constant across slice # Then it passes the variance check even though E01 is in mapping

title: LaTeX Generation
text: generating LaTeX optimized models, optimization summary automatically included: optimization summary includes: - Folding statistics: Number percentage folded parameters - Dimension reductions: Details folded parameter (e.g., 5D → 2D) - Trimming statistics: Counts trimmed sets, parameters, mappings, variables, equations - Explanatory text: Describes folding trimming
code: tex <- write_latex(model_optimized, model_view = "full")

title: LaTeX Generation
text: full view mode, folded parameters show green annotations:
code: # Parameters will show: (folded: 5D → 2D) in green tex <- write_latex(model_optimized, model_view = "full")

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Trimmed elements marked blue (customizable):
code: # Default blue color tex <- write_latex(model_optimized,                    model_view = "full",                    trimmed_color = "blue")  # Custom color tex <- write_latex(model_optimized,                    model_view = "full",                    trimmed_color = "red")

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Control whether show set elements parameter row counts:
code: # With data (default) tex <- write_latex(demo_model, include_data = TRUE)  # Without data (theory mode) tex <- write_latex(demo_model, include_data = FALSE)

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Control amount data shown:
code: # Brief: Shows row counts and first few elements tex <- write_latex(demo_model, data_detail = "brief")  # Detailed: Shows more information tex <- write_latex(demo_model, data_detail = "detailed")

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Customize set elements displayed:
code: tex <- write_latex(demo_model,                   set_display_max_inline = 10,        # Max elements to show inline                   set_display_head_tail_threshold = 100,  # Threshold for head/tail                   set_display_head_n = 5,             # Number of head elements                   set_display_tail_n = 3)             # Number of tail elements

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Index aliases provide short names dimensions equations: LaTeX output includes “Index Aliases” section showing mapping.
code: # Aliases are auto-detected from model$index_aliases tex <- write_latex(demo_model, use_model_aliases = TRUE)  # This will use 'c' instead of 'comm', 'r' instead of 'region', etc.

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Control aliases appear:
code: # Default: Full names in declarations, aliases in equations tex <- write_latex(demo_model, use_aliases_in_declarations = FALSE)  # Aliases everywhere tex <- write_latex(demo_model, use_aliases_in_declarations = TRUE)

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Control sections appear output:
code: tex <- write_latex(demo_model,                   include_sets = TRUE,                   include_aliases = TRUE,                   include_index_aliases = TRUE,                   include_parameters = TRUE,                   include_variables = TRUE,                   include_equations = TRUE,                   include_mappings = TRUE)  # Now TRUE by default  # Equations only tex <- write_latex(demo_model,                   include_sets = FALSE,                   include_parameters = FALSE,                   include_variables = FALSE,                   include_equations = TRUE)

title: LaTeX Generation
text: Add table contents document:
code: tex <- write_latex(demo_model, include_toc = TRUE)

title: multimod to Pyomo
text: Pyomo supports two model types. multimod uses AbstractModel: AbstractModel? Separation concerns: Model structure independent data Reusability: model code different datasets Debugging: Inspect model structure instantiation energyRt compatibility: Matches scenario-based workflow Testing: Easy validate small test datasets ConcreteModel (used) embeds data directly:
code: # AbstractModel (what we generate) model = AbstractModel() model.REGION = Set() model.YEAR = Set() model.pDiscountRate = Param(model.REGION, domain=Reals, default=0.05)  # Data loaded separately via DataPortal instance = model.create_instance(data) # ConcreteModel (not used) model = ConcreteModel() model.REGION = Set(initialize=['R1', 'R2'])  # Data embedded

title: multimod to Pyomo
text: generated Pyomo code uses best practices:
code: # Sets model.REGION = Set(doc="Regions") model.TECHNOLOGY = Set(doc="Technologies")  # Mappings (sets of tuples) model.mTechSpan = Set(dimen=2, doc="(technology, year)")  # Parameters with defaults and domains model.pDiscountRate = Param(model.REGION, default=0.05,                               domain=Reals, doc="Discount rate") model.pTechStock = Param(model.TECHNOLOGY, model.YEAR,                           default=0, domain=Reals)  # Variables with bounds model.vTechCap = Var(model.mTechSpan, within=NonNegativeReals) model.vObjective = Var(within=Reals)  # Free variable model.vBinaryChoice = Var(model.TECHNOLOGY, within=Binary)  # Constraints with rule functions def eqTechCap_rule(model, h, y):     if (h, y) not in model.mTechSpan:         return Constraint.Skip     return (         model.vTechCap[h, y] ==          model.pTechStock[h, y] +         sum(model.vTechNewCap[h, yy]              for yy in model.YEAR              if (h, yy, y) in model.mTechNew)     )  model.eqTechCap = Constraint(     model.TECHNOLOGY, model.YEAR,     rule=eqTechCap_rule )  # Objective model.objective = Objective(     rule=lambda model: model.vObjective,     sense=minimize )

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Energy system models face fundamental tradeoff: flexibility vs. computational efficiency.

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Modern energy system modeling frameworks like energyRt designed maximum flexibility mind: Generic structure: Hundreds pre-defined equations/constraints covering diverse technologies, storage, trade, emissions, etc. Multi-dimensional data: Parameters indexed across technology, commodity, region, year, time-slice, Universal applicability: framework works simple academic examples (UTOPIA) complex national models However, every scenario uses every feature: simple 1-region model doesn’t need interregional trade constraints Technologies don’t vary time-slice redundant data across slices Empty sets unused parameters create overhead solvers Constraints applicable data still get generated

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: flexibility creates computational overhead:
code: UTOPIA Model (unfold, untrimmed): ├─ 124 equations × ~500 instances each = ~62,000 potential constraints ├─ 70+ parameters with 5-6 dimensions each = ~50,000 data points ├─ Many equations generate no actual constraints (empty domains) └─ Result: Solver processes much more than needed

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: multimod provides two techniques eliminate redundancy: Folding - Reduces data redundancy collapsing constant dimensions Trimming - Removes unused model elements (empty sets, variables, equations) Together, can reduce model size 10-100x preserving solution accuracy.

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Many parameters constant across certain dimensions. Folding removes dimensions: equations reference folded parameter, dimension omitted:
code: # Original: pTechCinp2use indexed by 5 dimensions pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, SPRING] = 0.95 pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, SUMMER] = 0.95 pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, AUTUMN] = 0.95 pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025, WINTER] = 0.95  # After folding: Remove 'slice' dimension (constant value) pTechCinp2use[E01, ELC, R1, 2025] = 0.95  # Compression: 4 rows → 1 row (4x reduction) # Before: vTechInp[t,c,r,y,s] >= pTechCinp2use[t,c,r,y,s] * vTechAct[t,r,y,s] # After:  vTechInp[t,c,r,y,s] >= pTechCinp2use[t,c,r,y] * vTechAct[t,r,y,s]

text: Many model elements unused specific scenarios: Empty sets: data (e.g., storage technologies model) Empty parameters: rows (e.g., storage costs storage) Variables empty domains: Indexed empty sets Equations instances: domains empty Trimming marks $trimmed = TRUE code generators skip .

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Four-phase process: Phase 4 crucial - ensures don’t trim something ’s actually needed.
code: Phase 1: Mark empty data   └─ Sets, parameters, mappings with no data  Phase 2: Mark variables with empty domains   └─ Variables indexed by empty sets  Phase 3: Mark equations with empty domains   └─ Equations indexed by empty sets OR using only trimmed variables  Phase 4: Untrim required elements   └─ Anything used by non-trimmed equations gets untrimmed

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Use Folding : - Parameters constant values across dimensions (high redundancy) - Model fine-grained dimensions needed scenario - Want reduce data file size solver memory - Data bottleneck (large CSV/dat files) Use Trimming : - Model optional features used scenario - Empty sets parameters exist - Want reduce constraint generation overhead - Model structure bottleneck (many unused equations) Use : - Working flexible framework models (like energyRt) - Building scenario-specific optimized models - Solving large-scale models every optimization helps - Recommended workflow: Fold first, trim (folding may create new trim opportunities)

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Requires constant values: Data must truly identical across dimension --nothing: Can’t fold just instances parameter Mapping dependency: Needs validation mappings (entities vary) Memory cost: Folding process loads data memory Reversibility cost: Unfolding requires regenerating redundant data

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: structural redundancy: Doesn’t reduce data, elements Conservative design: Phase 4 prevents -trimming May miss opportunities: Unused variables detected (Phase 5 removed) Code generation dependent: Requires generator support $trimmed flag

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Don’t fold : - Values actually vary across dimension (corrupt model) - Dimension values (e.g., 2-3 slices - minimal benefit) - Working dynamic data may change - Debugging model (folded code harder trace) Don’t trim : - Model already minimal (like UTOPIA unfolded) - Need complete structure documentation - Comparing models (trimming makes structure incomparable) - Elements may become non-empty future scenarios

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Folding improves: - File /O (smaller data files) - Solver memory (fewer coefficients) - Network transfer (smaller files) Folding doesn’t improve: - Constraint count (equations, just different indexing) - Solve time much (structure unchanged) Trimming improves: - Code generation time (fewer elements process) - Constraint count (equations generated) - Solver preprocessing (fewer empty constraints) Trimming doesn’t improve: - Data size (structure removed, data) - File /O (data files unchanged)

title: Model Redundancy Elimination: Trimming and Folding
text: Folding trimming complementary - use maximum optimization Folding targets data redundancy (constant values across dimensions) Trimming targets structural redundancy (unused model elements) Results mathematically equivalent - objectives match original UTOPIA demonstrates effectiveness - 96x data compression + 12% fewer elements Start conservative, validate always - incremental folding verification

text: One optimization model, many representations. multimod R toolkit defining, translating, documenting, solving algebraic optimization models. stores model common abstract syntax tree (AST), separating mathematical structure one modeling language solver interface. shared representation, multimod can: inspect, validate, visualize, fold, trim, serialize model; render equations complete formulation LaTeX; generate GAMS, GMPL/MathProg, Julia/JuMP, Python/Pyomo, R code; bypass generated model code assemble solver-ready LP matrix directly, write MPS, solve -process HiGHS. package grew energy-system modeling, AST rendering machinery domain-independent.

title: Define and Render Mathematical Models Across Optimization Languages
text: Mathematical models often become coupled language first written. multimod separates three concerns: Model meaning — sets, parameters, variables, mappings, equations, objectives AST. Representation — human-readable LaTeX, executable backend code, JSON, sparse LP/MPS matrix. Execution — local solver, institutional modeling environment, remote hardware. separation makes possible compare backends, document exact model solved, manipulate execution, reuse one formulation across several solver ecosystems.

Supply a validation mapping for this dimension to confirm they are unreachable. #> 2       Values are constant, but the parameter never indexes 5 of 17 timeslice members (ANNUAL, FAL, SPR), which resolve to the default. Supply a validation mapping for this dimension to confirm they are unreachable. #> 3 Values are constant, but the parameter never indexes 16 of 17 timeslice members (FAL, FAL_DAY, FAL_NGT), which resolve to the default. title: Fold model dimensions to reduce data size — fold_model
text: algorithm uses per-group validation: combination dimensions, checks values identical. "nothing" approach - group shows variation, dimension folded. Folding analyzes parameter identify dimensions provide variation data. parameter, groups dimensions checks values constant within group (within tolerance). Example: pStorageInpEff[stg, comm, region, year, timeslice] testing timeslice: Groups (stg, comm, region, year) group, checks timeslice values identical folds EVERY group constant values handles sparse data correctly - parameter values peak hours (1 timeslice 17), fine. checks values exist constant within group. fold creates three slots per parameter: data: Original complete data (preserved) folded_data: Collapsed data reduced dimensions active_dims: Dimensions remaining fold Safety measures: folds dimensions explicitly requested user Never folds structural dimensions (tech, comm, sup, dem, stg, trade, etc.) Skips parameters dimensions folded (become scalar) Validates consistency folding Updates equation ASTs match reduced dimensions

code: # Julia source of the save_solution() helper embedded in generated model.jl cat(write_jump_solution_code()) #>  #> # Function to save solution values #> function save_solution(model, output_dir, data_format) #>     using Dates #>     using DataFrames #>     using CSV #>     using Arrow #>      #>     if !isdir(output_dir) #>         mkpath(output_dir) #>     end #>      #>     println("\nSaving solution to: ", output_dir) #>      #>     # Determine file extension #>     ext = data_format == "csv" ? ".csv" : ".arrow" #>      #>     # Save each variable #>     for (var_name, var_obj) in object_dict(model) #>         if !(var_obj isa AbstractArray{VariableRef}) #>             continue #>         end #>          #>         # Get variable values #>         var_vals = value.(var_obj) #>          #>         # Convert to DataFrame based on dimensions #>         if var_obj isa DenseAxisArray #>             # Get indices #>             indices = axes(var_obj) #>             n_dims = length(indices) #>              #>             if n_dims == 0 #>                 # Scalar variable #>                 df = DataFrame(value = [var_vals]) #>             else #>                 # Multi-dimensional variable #>                 idx_names = [Symbol("dim$i") for i in 1:n_dims] #>                 rows = [] #>                  #>                 for idx in Iterators.product(indices...) #>                     val = var_vals[idx...] #>                     if abs(val) > 1e-10  # GAMS output compiles: $ conditions bracketed, descriptions containing comma quoted, dims tuple double-wrapped, equation headers bind domain’s dims, unary operator reads operand $rhs. fold_model() refuses fold dimension parameter never indexes members validation mapping shows unreachable. Folding one broadcast stored value default applied. fold_equations() now rewrites parameter references inside unary operator. vExportRowCost = -sum{...} two three terms eqSubsCost kept unfolded arity, MathProg rejects JuMP Pyomo accepted silently substituting default weight. fold_model() refuses dimension parameter carries , timeslice pTimesliceAgg(year, timeslice, timeslicep) region pTradeIr* family. declaration rewrite reference rewrite drop every matching dimension, folding collapsed pair one subscript.
